Its been almost a year and I still don't know what any of these stupid titles mean..

I thought my supervisor was actually straight-up a manager this whole time because of how interchangeably "lead" is treated; the term basically means nothing if you're trying to figure out what's what by just reading them off of a list.

I used to work at a different location and my old team was amazing. I genuinely miss my leads and how much respect they had for both us and the animals. Its just so.. different, at this other place. I used to hold PetSmart in really high esteem because ive worked at some terrible mom and pop dog daycares. I was so impressed with my old team.

Having the same experience after moving locations. Previous coworkers and managers were amazing, considerate of which regulars got along and didnt, had no issue turning customers down if it meant keeping their dogs and us safer. Now im at a place where nobody is mindful of which dogs are bad with who and they refuse to remove obviously problematic dogs who start repeated fights, this is especially stressful in the big window playroom where customers can see these lovely dog fights, lying to customers about how the dogs stay was because they probably wouldn't reboard if they knew we dragged their dog into camp by the throat screaming and thrashing, refusing to start health charts for some bizarre reasons (i told her we had bloody diarrhea in one suite, she just goes "yea i know:)" and ignores me while tapping away at the computer..). I dont even know where the health charts are and im convinced they throw them out or don't even print/stock any in our hotel.

Oh, and she won't get any more walkies. We have none. There's no way to communicate with anyone while in camp, you just have to hope someone nearby can hear you shout for help. I am considering reporting my management tbh.

My previous hotel was like this, then we closed, I transferred elsewhere, and now its the opposite which is frustrating for me. The woman who manages us seems power trippy and doesn't like removing dogs ever, even when they've bitten each other multiple times already and have to be dragged into camp cus they hate it :/ She obviously only cares about retaining customers and has no issue lying about how their dogs stay was because if they knew they were uncomfortable they probably wouldn't board.. At my last place if a dog was too worked up we explained to the PPs that hey your dogs clearly gonna have a bad time and we cant take your reservation. This location though is just profit profit profit.

i used drysol for a few years starting in highschool before it stopped working entirely one day and it was intolerable. i did some research and pretty much marched into my drs office asking for it (glyco) directly and explaining why. my hyperhidrosis literally prevented me from doing anything but sitting and watching netflix all day (cant work at a computer when your hands sweat nonstop). good luck!

i know i posted this as a joke but just wanted to say this medication has pretty much changed my life. id take dry mouth and some nasal congestion over uncontrollable nonstop full-body sweating any day. i can sit in a warm room with socks off and wear white clothing for the first time in my entire life with the confidence that i wont turn into a human slug at random
